text:
mira_support: Customer (ACME) in prod reporting JSON-mode function call failures since 09:03 UTC. They say the same payload worked yesterday. Error: \"function_call_validation_failed: missing required property 'order_id'\". Marking P1, need eng oncall.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-9832 linked, customer plan: paid.

sam_engineering: Can you paste the exact request body + function schema? Also which SDK/version and model?

mira_support: Pasting minimal repro and response (redacted customer PII):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"create order"}],"functions":[{"name":"create_order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"quantity":{"type":"integer"}}},"required":["id","quantity"]}},"required":["order_id","items"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"create_order"}}'
```

Response (400):
```json
{"error":{"code":"function_call_validation_failed","message":"Missing required property 'order_id' at /functions[0]/arguments"}}
```

mira_support: Customer payload they actually sent (they claim):
```json
{"action":"create_order","args":{"items":[{"sku":"ABC123","qty":2}],"shipping":{"address":"..."}}}
```

alex_oncall: I see two mismatch vectors: (1) function schema expects items[].id and items[].quantity, but client sends sku/qty keys; (2) order_id is required by schema but client sends none. Are we validating strictly in JSON mode? Any transformation on our side?

sam_engineering: We validate arguments against the declared function schema server-side before invoking tool routing. If required props missing -> 400. Usually customers pass a stringified JSON in the top-level "arguments" field for older clients.

mira_support: Customer says they upgraded client yesterday (they upgraded internal mapping). They think schema didn't change. Request id: req_0a9f3b2e. Attached logs from their side show the payload above.

sam_engineering: Can you ask for the function registration payload they passed (the functions array)? Might be a mismatch between what they registered and what they think is registered. Also which SDK - is it our node SDK v1.4.0? That one changed default json_mode to "strict" in last minor.

mira_support: They confirmed Node SDK 1.4.0. They registered a function with older property names (sku/qty) but our runtime validated against the published schema (id/quantity). I suspect schema drift: their local mapping updated but function schema in the request still lists id/quantity, so their args dont match. They say it worked yesterday though.

alex_oncall: Two action items: (A) give customer a quick workaround: send arguments as a single string (legacy path) or map keys client-side to match the function schema. Recommend sending a minimal shim: {"order_id":"temp-<ts>","items":[{"id":"ABC123","quantity":2}]}. (B) Eng to verify whether changing default json_mode to strict caused this sudden break for recent SDK users.

sam_engineering: I pulled the server log for req_0a9f3b2e: 
```
validate_arguments(req_0a9f3b2e): path=/functions[0]/arguments, error=Missing required property 'order_id'
parse_mode_check: json_mode=strict
```
Looks like strict validation triggered. We can consider a mitigation: allow lenient validation for customers on paid plans for a short window, but need caution.

mira_support: Customer is stuck in production flow, billing unaffected but feature blocked. They asked for ETA and temporary bypass.

sam_engineering: Short-term: encourage the shim. I'll prototype a server-side tolerance flag that accepts missing required fields if the incoming body includes an explicit "_raw_arguments" string field (we already support legacy stringified arguments). Medium-term: add clearer docs and a changelog note about SDK 1.4.0 default. Long-term: add a best-effort key-mapping helper in SDKs. I'll try to have a prototype PR by EOD and a canary rollback if risky.

alex_oncall: Assigning escalation -> tag incident-ops and schedule a quick sync with platform PM. Mira, please send the shim example to the customer and request they try immediately. Sam, keep me posted on PR link.

support-bot: Customer notified via email template. Ticket updated: INC-9832 -> status: escalated.

mira_support: Sent workaround and asked them to test. Will report back within 30m. :crossed_fingers:

sam_engineering: I'll start a small repro using Node SDK 1.4.0 with json_mode=strict and the mismatched keys. If I can reproduce locally, I'll open a hotfix PR to relax validation for the legacy string-arguments path.

alex_oncall: Thanks — please post PR and ETA here. If customer still blocked after 30m escalate to SRE for a quick config flip on their org id to allow lenient parsing.

mira_support: Customer confirmed workaround works for them (added order_id and remapped keys). They can proceed for now but would like a permanent fix. Closing immediate blocker; leaving escalation open until eng provides a timeline.

sam_engineering: Noted. PR draft will be up within 4 hours. I'll include e2e test that covers both legacy string args and strict JSON mode.

alex_oncall: Great. Adding follow-up action: add changelog entry and email to customers who upgraded to SDK 1.4.0.

support-bot: Incident INC-9832 -> followups scheduled.
